workflow_rules.text: Raw well-log interpretation must start with data inventory, unit checks, depth ordering, sampling consistency, missing-value analysis, borehole-condition screening and range checks before any geological inference.

Borehole and environmental effects must be evaluated before lithology, porosity and saturation interpretation; enlarged holes, mudcake, invasion and tool-specific corrections can invalidate direct curve-response rules.

Multi-curve interpretation requires strictly monotonic depth, consistent sampling interval and depth alignment among curves; conflicted depths must be corrected or flagged before crossplot or model inference.

Short isolated gaps may be interpolated after QC, but extended missing AC, CNL/NEU, density or resistivity intervals must be imputed with documented uncertainty or sent to expert review before dependent interpretation.
Lithology and matrix assumptions must be established before porosity and reservoir-parameter prediction because density, neutron and sonic porosity transforms depend on matrix and shale corrections.

Water saturation must not be interpreted from resistivity alone; it requires porosity, formation-water resistivity or an equivalent calibration, lithology/shale assessment and a selected saturation equation.
Fluid identification must integrate porosity, water saturation, deep/shallow resistivity behavior, invasion evidence and lithology; no single log response is sufficient for a final fluid conclusion.

The final report must preserve input provenance, curve availability, preprocessing actions, selected interpretation equations or models, physical validation results, abnormal intervals and expert-review flags.

quality_control.constraint: Record which essential curves are available before planning. Lithology, porosity, saturation and fluid tasks must expose degraded confidence when their preferred curves are absent.
Large CAL-BS separation indicates washout or borehole enlargement; density and neutron porosity in those intervals should be corrected, down-weighted or reviewed.
Resistivity curves must be positive before logarithmic scaling, saturation calculation or invasion analysis.
SP interpretation requires shale baseline and sand-line context; absolute SP magnitude alone should not be treated as a fluid or permeability conclusion.

lithology.constraint: High gamma ray generally indicates shale content, while low gamma ray suggests cleaner formations; radioactive sands, feldspar or potassium-rich minerals require cross-checks.

Density-neutron response and photoelectric factor should be used to separate sandstone, limestone and dolomite when available; matrix-sensitive curves must not be interpreted without lithology context.
SP deflection can support identification of permeable beds, but it depends on mud filtrate and formation-water salinity and must be combined with GR and resistivity.

porosity.constraint: Density porosity requires matrix density and fluid density assumptions selected from lithology and borehole conditions.
Neutron porosity is affected by hydrogen index, shale-bound water and gas; density-neutron crossover or disagreement must trigger gas/shale/environment review.
Sonic porosity needs matrix transit time and may require compaction correction; it should be cross-validated against density or neutron porosity where possible.
Final porosity should reconcile available density, neutron and sonic estimates after shale and borehole corrections, not blindly average inconsistent curves.

shale_volume.constraint: GR-derived shale volume must be bounded to 0-1 and should use local clean-sand and shale baselines rather than global minima and maxima when calibration data exist.
Shale volume inferred from GR should be cross-checked with SP and neutron-density behavior in intervals where radioactive minerals or borehole effects are suspected.

saturation.constraint: Archie saturation is appropriate for relatively clean formations; high VSH or conductive clay requires a shaly-sand model or expert review.
Saturation output should expose the assumed cementation exponent, saturation exponent, tortuosity factor and formation-water resistivity when those parameters are not calibrated.
Water and hydrocarbon saturations must remain in 0-1 and should not exceed a total pore-volume fraction of 1 after rounding.

fluid_identification.constraint: Deep/shallow resistivity separation can support invasion and movable-fluid interpretation, but it must be checked against porosity, saturation and mud-filtrate context.
Intervals with very low effective porosity should not be classified as productive fluid layers solely because resistivity is high.
Potential gas effect indicated by density-neutron separation, high resistivity and low neutron response should be flagged separately from oil-water classification.
